chunks: Among his proofs (peace be upon him) is that he said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not make for people in their deeds any proof except through an Imam who guides them or a Messenger who warns them.
ai.seo_question: What is the basis for the validity of human deeds in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this pivotal hadith to establish the theological necessity of the Imamate as a prerequisite for the validity of worship and deeds. This narration underscores the Shia doctrine that divine guidance requires an infallible guide (Ma'sum) to interpret and implement Sharia, thereby preventing arbitrary interpretation and ensuring the continuity of prophetic authority after the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
